lines.japanese: よし、ここはせっかくだから喰わず嫌いせずに勉強させてもらおうかな。針生さんも言ってた、面白いものはそこら中にあるからよく探してみろって。僕は趣味に対して、もっとオープンになるべきなんだ。
lines.english: All right, I had the chance, so maybe I should stop judging before I tried it and learn something. Hariu had said it too: interesting stuff was lying all over the place, so I should keep my eyes open. I needed to be more open to different hobbies.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあさ、山科さんの一番お勧めっていうと、どのバンドなのかな」
lines.english: “So, Yamashina—if you had to pick your number-one recommendation, which band would it be?”

lines.japanese: 「一番？　一番ならいくつかあるけど、どの一番？　一番の中でも一番ってこと？　それとも一番好きなのを全部あげろってこと？」
lines.english: “Number one? I have several number ones. Which number one do you mean? The number one of all my number ones? Or do you want every single one of the bands I like best?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、じゃあ、ええと一番の中の一番かな」
lines.english: “Th-then... um, the number one of the number ones.”

lines.japanese: もにゅっ。山科さんが僕の背中にひときわ強く体を押しつけた。というか、飛びあがって天井から吊るされたモニターを指差した。
lines.english: Squoosh. Yamashina pressed herself particularly hard against my back—or rather, she jumped up and pointed at a monitor suspended from the ceiling.

lines.japanese: 「やっぱりＫｕＲｉＹａかな、だってね、ＫｕＲｉＹａはね、私が一番最初に目を付けてたんだもん。間違いないよ一番だよ、私ってひとの才能を見抜く目に秀でてるからね、ＫｕＲｉＹａは来ると思ってたんだ」
lines.english: “I guess it has to be KuRiYa! See, I was the very first one to spot KuRiYa. No question, number one. I have a special gift for recognizing talent, you know. I always knew KuRiYa would make it.”

lines.japanese: 「言ってみれば私がＫｕＲｉＹａを育てたようなものだよね。今はメジャーになっちゃったけど最初から応援してたからね、もう生みの親より育ての親ってやつだよ私とＫｕＲｉＹａ最高！　主に私最高！」
lines.english: “You could practically say I raised KuRiYa myself. KuRiYa has gone major now, but I was there from the very beginning. The parent who raises you matters more than the one who gives birth! KuRiYa and me—the best! Mostly me!”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、そうなんだ。山科さんの眼鏡に適うっていうのはすごいことなんだね」
lines.english: “I see. Winning Yamashina’s seal of approval must be quite an achievement.”

lines.japanese: 「やだそんなことないけど、でもでも確かに私が目をつけたバンドは大体メジャーデビューするっていうか？　皆より一歩先に進んでるっていうか？」
lines.english: “Oh, I’m not that special. Though I guess almost every band I notice ends up making a major-label debut? You might say I’m always one step ahead of everybody else?”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、山科さんってプロデューサーの才能があるのかもね」
lines.english: “Maybe you have the makings of a producer, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな、羽田君の言うことに微塵の間違いもないけど、あんまりにも誉めすぎだよ。あ、じゃあ羽田君もプロデュースしてあげよっか？　汰架示ｆｅａｔ．瑠樺！　どう？　よくない？」
lines.english: “Oh, Haneda, not a word of that was wrong, but you flatter me too much! Wait—want me to produce you too? Takashi feat. Ruka! What do you think? Isn’t it great?”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう。でもおれ、音楽の道に進むつもりはないんだ」
lines.english: “Thank you. But I don’t plan on going into music.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー残念だなぁ。でもその気になったらいつでも言ってね」
lines.english: “Aww, what a shame. If you ever change your mind, just tell me.”

lines.japanese: そこまで言ってもらえるのはお世辞でも嬉しかったけど、ごめんね山科さん、僕はそう遠くない将来グレタガルドへ旅立ってしまうと思うから。
lines.english: Even if she was just being polite, I was happy to hear it. But sorry, Yamashina. I thought I'd be leaving for Gretagard before too long.

lines.japanese: けれど彼女はまだ諦めきれず、なんとか僕を歌手デビューさせようと様々な誘い文句を唱えつづける。どうも違う話題を振ってごまかすしかなさそうだ。
lines.english: She was not ready to give up, however, and kept trying every pitch she could think of to launch my singing career. It seemed my only escape was to distract her with another subject.
